title: OSINT API: how to build open-source research into your tools
summary: What an OSINT API is and how to use one: send a name, email, phone or company, and Sixtyfour returns the fields you ask for, each with its source URL.
body_markdown:
An OSINT API takes an identifier, such as a name, email address, phone number, username or company, and returns what open sources say about it, with the source each answer came from. The kinds developers meet are record lookups that return what a stored database holds, web search APIs that return matching pages, and research agents that read sources and return cited answers. Pick by the question: standard fields at volume, pages to read yourself, or answers someone will check.


Yes. Sixtyfour's People Intelligence and Company Intelligence endpoints take what you know about a subject and the fields you want, research sources across the web and return those fields with the pages they were read on, plus a 0 to 100 confidence score for each field if you ask. Its Reverse Lookup endpoint finds the person behind an email address or phone number, and Atlas, enabled on request, runs a full investigation with an attribution graph. Anything the research could not establish comes back empty for a person on your team to decide.


Open-source OSINT tools on GitHub are free to run, and you host and maintain them yourself. Sixtyfour charges credits for research and lookups, and as of November 2026 checking a job, reading its results, checking your balance, per-field confidence scores and a contact lookup that finds no result cost nothing. Research starts at 0.3 credits a person at the micro tier.


With Sixtyfour, sign in to the web app, open API Keys in Settings, create a key with a name and an expiry, and copy it, because the full key is shown only once. Send it in the x-api-key header on every request and keep it on your server. For machine-to-machine integrations that need short-lived tokens, an OAuth client can exchange a signed assertion for a Bearer token instead.


A web search API returns pages that match a query and leaves you to decide which ones describe your subject. An OSINT research API does that step for you: it returns answers about one person or company with the pages each answer rests on, and says how sure it is. Many investigation tools use search to find pages and research to attribute facts.


Send them in one batch request instead of one call each. Sixtyfour's Intelligence endpoints take up to 100,000 records inline or an uploaded CSV, JSON, JSONL or NDJSON file, each record with your own custom_id, and you read the results page by page or receive them by webhook. Polling is limited to 300 status reads a minute per organisation, enough for about 50 jobs in flight at one poll every 10 seconds.


Store every value with the URL it was read on, the query that produced it and the time it was asked. Keep a field that came back empty apart from one a source contradicts, because finding nothing is evidence of neither. Run the research again before a decision instead of relying on an old answer.
